plannerAnswers.question: What did you like most about this prompt?
plannerAnswers.answer: It sets firm outcomes and leaves the creative calls open. The brief says what must exist (a feature-complete slice, dev mode, attract mode, hub play, a 10-foot UI, no stubs) and lets the director choose genre, camera and scope. The 'This computer' section was the most useful part: exact browsers, flags, memory behaviour and shared-machine rules, plus an honest list of what this machine lacks and what to test with instead. That made it possible to prove things before planning them. 'Build it without you' was a good constraint too, because it pushed me to run the risky parts and hand over working facts instead of guesses. Wii Fit was also a good source to pick: its identity is a physical peripheral, so a recreation is not even possible and the game has to be a real translation.

plannerAnswers.question: What was confusing?
plannerAnswers.answer: 1) 'Follow the hub README for multiplayer integration into ai-hub as well as for the game on its own'. The README only covers hub sessions and says the game is unaffected outside one, so 'on its own' could mean plain solo play or local multiplayer. I planned same-screen Group Class to be safe. 2) TASK.md is written to the builder, so as planner I had to decide which parts applied to me. I treated Source Information, the feedback sections and the exit interview as the builder's. 3) Nothing says whether a planner may build and run things. I assumed yes and kept throwaway probes in a scratch folder, which I removed. 4) 'Performance budget unlimited' conflicts with one hard limit: the hub harness gives each copy 20 s to call ready(), and on software WebGPU the engine's own playground takes 52-73 s at four copies. 5) 'Music at 10%' does not say of what. I took it as the music bus at 0.1, under a master at its 0.7 default. 6) The brief does not say how large a build the plan should assume, or which model will build it, so I added a cut line instead of knowing the scope.

plannerAnswers.question: What was the hardest thing to do?
plannerAnswers.answer: Designing how the game feels without being able to feel it. Wii Fit is your whole body on a balance board. The plan has to make a thumbstick carry that, and neither I nor the builders have hands or a display here. My first balance tuning looked reasonable on paper, but a simulation with a 250 ms human-like reaction showed that doing nothing beat actively correcting, because correction that late amplifies a 0.45 Hz sway. Slowing the sway fixed it (no input 38%, human-like thumb 90%), and that led to a test idea I put in the plan: delayed-thumb bots stand in for players. The other hard part was finding what the engine really allows, since the most important facts were not in its docs: the page has no access to the scene, and it cannot switch scenes while running. Worst of all, the hub's query string kills createEngine while the hub harness still reports PASS. I only found these by running things.

plannerAnswers.question: What would you change in this prompt?
plannerAnswers.answer: 1) Add to 'This computer': set CHROMIUM_PATH to the downloaded chromium_headless_shell binary. The engine's browser tools crash without it and then hang, and the full chrome binary dies with 'Socket path too long' because of the run's long TMPDIR. Also say not to run the engine's scripts/setup.sh, which downloads Node and Chromium outside the folder. 2) Warn about the hub and engine trap: the hub opens the page with ?aihub=1&aihub-seed=N, createEngine treats unknown query keys as settings and fails, and the harness still passes. Better still, fix it in the engine, and have the harness check that the game is actually running. 3) Say plainly what 'on its own' multiplayer requires. 4) State the builder's budget or expected size, so a plan can be scoped to it rather than hedged. 5) Split TASK.md into what the planner must use and what only the builder must do, or give the planner a shorter version. 6) Say whether a planner may prototype. 7) Note that the engine gives a game no one-file build, since x html is engine-only, though the brief requires a single HTML, and that 'node x new' reports failure in a game workspace because of a docs check on paths a game does not ship. These are small engine fixes that would save every builder the same discovery.
